svg.text: Глава 10 · Ethernet в локальных сетях
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0287:c01–p0325:c01 · PDF 287–325 · printed 286–324
1 · Shared-medium Ethernet
One medium shared by all nodes → capacity and access are collective
CSMA/CD → sense carrier · transmit · detect collision · jam · random retry
Minimum frame duration must cover worst-case collision round trip
Hub/repeater changes physical topology, not logical shared-medium semantics
Historical model explains frame-size legacy; modern Ethernet does not rely on collisions
2 · MAC / frame invariants
IEEE 802 → physical + MAC + LLC decomposition
MAC address → individual/group/broadcast + globally/local administered
Ethernet II → DA · SA · EtherType · payload · CRC-32/FCS
Promiscuous mode accepts frames regardless of destination MAC for observation
MAC/frame structure largely survives the transition to high-speed switched Ethernet
3 · Transparent bridge / switch
Learn source MAC → ingress port continuously
Known destination on another port → forward
Known destination on same port → filter
Unknown / broadcast / group → flood to all except ingress
Dynamic entries age; static entries can override default behavior
Loops cause duplication, indefinite circulation and MAC-table instability
4 · Switched full-duplex architecture
Microsegmentation → one endpoint per switch port
Full duplex → simultaneous TX/RX without collision semantics
Parallel port processing → aggregate throughput above one-link rate
Output contention still queues when several inputs target one port
ASIC / FPGA / NPU + matrix/bus/shared memory form the forwarding engine
Nonblocking requires end-to-end internal capacity, not just fast port PHYs
5 · Modular high-speed PHY
RS → adapts MAC interface · PCS → logical coding/FEC functions
PMA → serialize/deserialize + clock recovery · PMD → medium signaling
Autonegotiation selects mutually supported speed/duplex
Fast/Gigabit → 4B/5B, MLT-3, 8B/10B, 4D-PAM5 examples
The MAC model stays comparatively stable while PHY techniques change
6 · 10G → 800G scaling
10G+ → full-duplex-only source model
40/100G → 64B/66B + multiple parallel lanes
200/400G → PAM4 gives 2 bits/symbol; Reed–Solomon FEC restores margin
Later 400/800G → faster lanes reduce required lane/wavelength count
Coherent Ethernet/DWDM source examples trade higher cost for long reach
Operational reading rule
First identify the model: shared/half-duplex, learning switch behavior, or high-speed PHY/lane/FEC problem.
Then verify speed/duplex → FDB learning/movement → flooding/loops/queues → PHY and optics.
No executable CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 11 starts at p0326:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
